messages:
Maria Chen: psa — seeing a bunch of tiny-pod evictions in us-west2c. Pods go Pending -> FailedScheduling even though some nodes show free GPUs. Suspect a rack NIC hotspot + scheduler packing rules.
Ajay Patel: can you paste the `kubectl describe pod` events for one example?
Maria Chen: sure — sample events:
```
Events:
  Type     Reason             Age   From               Message
  ----     ------             ----  ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling   2m    default-scheduler  0/20 nodes are available: 5 node(s) had taint {gpu: true}, 10 node(s) had diskPressure, 3 node(s) had insufficient resources, 2 node(s) failed predicate, 5 node(s) MatchNodeSelector failed.
```
Ajay Patel: hmm ok. Those "failed predicate" lines + taints look generic. Any recent scheduler changes rolled?
Trent O'Neil: we saw rack-23 NIC rx errors last night; if the scheduler scoring penalizes nodes by recent network load, it could shy away from packing on that rack and leave many tiny pods fragmented across racks.
Maria Chen: affinity/requests: nodeSelector: zone=us-west2c, tolerations: gpu:NoSchedule, requests: cpu 0.5, memory 2Gi, nvidia.com/gpu: 1 — many tiny 1-GPU jobs landing and leaving holes. No topologySpread constraints.
Sasha (infra-bot): Alert: rack-23 nic_rx_errors spiked 2026-03-20T22:10Z -> 22:45Z across nodes (ids: node-23a,node-23b). See perf logs.
Emily Davis: FYI we rolled the "network-aware topology scorer" last week (rollout id: sched-2026-03-18-v2). It reduces score for nodes with recent link saturation. Might be interacting badly with GPU binpacking.
Ajay Patel: can you canary-disable the scorer in that AZ and see if scheduling improves? Rolling back globally is heavy.
Maria Chen: did a canary flip on cluster us-west2c-rack-24, pods scheduled and started normally for ~30 min. Can confirm difference.
Trent O'Neil: sounds like the scorer is overly punitive for short NIC blips. Two follow-ups: 1) open a network ticket for rack-23, 2) tune scorer to look at 5m average not 30s.
Maria Chen: opened NET-4821 with dumps and dmesg, linked: <https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/NET-4821|NET-4821>. Assigned to @ops-oncall.
ops-oncall: I'm on it. Will run synthetic TCP/hyperscan load against rack-23 tonight. Meanwhile recommend temporarily rolling back sched-2026-03-18-v2 in us-west2c until we have a safe scoring window.
Emily Davis: +1 but note: relaxing scoring will pack more GPUs per rack and could raise thermal/egress hotspots. We should stagger rollback to avoid thermal spike.
Ajay Patel: cost note: if we force cross-rack packing to avoid this, egress costs go up. Better to fix scoring and NIC.
Maria Chen: plan: 1) rollback scorer in us-west2c (canary -> AZ -> cluster) 2) add a per-rack NIC-util cap in scheduler (reject nodes if recent util > 70%), 3) run synthetic to validate, 4) reintroduce tuned scoring. I'll post timeline in NET-4821.
Trent O'Neil: also add a short-lived admission controller check to limit simultaneous starts on a rack while we validate. Low-effort safety net.
ops-oncall: starting rollback now for canary AZ. Will update when done.
Maria Chen: thanks — will watch eviction count and post a short summary in #incidents if things look stable. :thumbsup:
Emily Davis: once stable, let's add a regression test in the scheduler e2e that simulates NIC blips + many tiny GPU jobs to catch this before rollout.
Maria Chen: agreed.
